Benign mucus-retention cyst of the uterine cervix, a reproductive organ outside the axes.

Intestinal ischemic disease defined by inadequate vascular supply and injury to the small or large bowel.

Benign hyaline-cartilage neoplasm arising in bone or soft tissue.
Flattening or damage of the pituitary gland defines the condition; its location at the brain base does not establish neural injury.
Cardiocutaneous disease; emphysema and intracranial hemorrhage each annotated 80-99%. Lipid abnormalities omitted by cap; associated cancers are separate diseases.
Viral infection defined by vascular injury and hemorrhagic/hemostatic dysfunction; specific visceral injuries vary across the umbrella.
Carcinoma directly occupies bone; the primary site is unspecified and cannot be assigned an additional axis.
Neuronal channelopathy causing ataxia and peripheral nerve hyperexcitability; spasms, visual symptoms and vertigo do not establish separate organ damage.
Neoplasm arising in glands of the anal canal.
Lysosomal storage disorder defined by neurodegeneration, seizures and vision loss from retinal degeneration.
Pontocerebellar malformation; congenital contractures in 2/4 and frequent arthrogryposis support joint involvement. Central apnea reflects brainstem dysfunction.
Infantile epilepsy syndrome; remission does not change its neurologic classification. Later epilepsy or dyskinesia adds no other axis.
Umbrella chiefly represented by breast fibroadenoma and phyllodes tumors, outside the axes; fibrous histology alone does not imply locomotor disease or justify the renal subtype.
